chapter: The union and the 1920s-30s band scene
title: Happy Johnson, Andy Anderson and Bob Dorsey
summary: Collette fishes for names; Howard recalls Happy Johnson as a Texas trombonist and Bob Dorsey as a good tenor player, but few details.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Let's see, there's somebody else we've -- what about Happy Johnson and that group?
Happy Johnson? Happy came from someplace down in Texas. Played trombone.
Weren't they some of the first blacks from around here to go to Japan or someplace like that?
Yeah, uh-huh. He played trombone.
That's right.
Happy Johnson. (Laughter)
Huh?
Happy. I can remember, a lot of things I can't remember about those fellows, but I know them all.
Oh, yeah. Do you remember any of those guys that went on a trip to Japan?
Where, to -- with Happy
(Inaudible.)
No, I don't remember who they were. Can't remember. I sure am sorry, too.
Do you remember Andy Anderson and people like that?
Andy Anderson. That name sounded
familiar.
Bob Dorsey?
Bob -- that name -- I knew Bob Dorsey.
He was a tenor player.
Yeah, tenor player. Good one, too.
Any of those guys -- do you remember anything about them?
No. They all seem to get out --
